chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskān, from al-Ḥalabī, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) about two money-changers who purchased silver (waraq) with gold dinars. One of them said to his partner, 'Settle [the debt] for me,' and he was wealthy; if he wished to settle, he would settle, so he settled for him. Then it occurred to him that he should buy his partner's share with a profit. Is it permissible? He said, 'There is no harm in it.'

key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ: There is no harm in it (permissible)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for one partner in a currency trade to buy out the other's share using profit?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates a specific currency exchange (*sarf*) scenario where one partner settles the other's debt and subsequently purchases their share with profit, ruling it permissible (*lā ba'sa*). This highlights the Shia juristic flexibility in commercial partnerships, distinguishing between the initial debt settlement and the subsequent profit-driven acquisition of equity. The ruling underscores the importance of clear intent and the absence of riba (usury) in layered financial transactions among partners.
